_comment: Provisional Assamese tokenizer. Trained on a 5% document sample of the assembled corpus for the sole purpose of measuring characters-per-token per source, so the mix can be planned in TOKENS rather than characters. This model is not a Phase 1 deliverable and is not used for training data.
_sample_rate_note: Telugu sampled 2% of a 2.29B character corpus, giving ~46M characters. The Assamese corpus is 1.11B characters, so 5% draws a comparable absolute sample (~55M characters) rather than a comparable fraction. What the measurement needs is enough text per source for a stable characters-per-token ratio, which is an absolute quantity.
_vocab_size_note: Provisional only. Set near the vocabulary size the sweep is expected to select for a corpus this size, so the measured characters-per-token is close to what the final tokenizer will deliver. The mix decision is barely sensitive to this: a systematic shift applies to every source alike, and the allocation depends on the ratios between sources.
_max_sentence_length_note: SentencePiece's limit is in BYTES and defaults to 4,192. Assamese costs three bytes per character in the Bengali-Assamese block, so the exporter's 2,000-character chunks reach ~6,000 bytes and would be dropped SILENTLY. On Telugu that silently discarded 0.72% of lines but 7.15% of the text, weighted towards the longest prose.
